claims.text: The initial material is stainless steel with a standard surface finish.
Passivation can significantly improve the corrosion resistance of stainless steel in extreme environments.
Coating stainless steel with corrosion-resistant materials can significantly improve its corrosion resistance in extreme environments.
The proposed treatment is passivation or application of a protective coating.
The relevant corrosive environments include high-chloride, acidic, or alkaline conditions.
Surface modification produces a modified surface layer.
The modified surface layer enhances the protective oxide layer or supplies a barrier against corrosive agents.
Passivation enhances formation of a stable protective oxide layer.
A protective coating creates a physical barrier that prevents corrosive substances from reaching the underlying metal.
The modified stainless steel will have a lower corrosion rate than untreated stainless steel under the same extreme corrosive conditions.
The treatment effects occur only in extreme corrosive environments and not in neutral or benign conditions.
The magnitude of corrosion-resistance improvement varies with the surface-modification technique and the corrosive environment.
